themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and no one can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Across cross-channel journey orchestration the models say channel owners with separate revenue targets will not give up a send, in agentic traffic they propose fast lanes and better prices so agents gain by declaring themselves, and in the semantic context layer all three call conflicting definitions a political settlement rather than a modeling gap.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: In answer engine optimization the models say model drift swings results more than any work they do, in cross-channel incrementality they say platforms adapt to the holdout, in identity resolution they recruit consenting panels to get a truth set, and in B2B buying-group signal loss they say a signal that decayed and a signal that was never real look identical.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models say black-box ad platforms and already-trained models offer no person-level proof, and in cross-channel incrementality they note the platforms control both the treatment and the evidence about it.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance the models restrict writing to pre-approved claims because software cannot judge implied meaning, and on the semantic context layer they argue a single definition of customer is the wrong target and only forced disclosure of which definition was used can work.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three route writes through a proxy or gateway with hard spend and audience caps, on downstream consent they funnel every data exit through a single checkpoint, and on journey orchestration they build one shared contact log or kill-switch list every channel must check before sending.
